tagline: Today's AI news, traced back to its roots.

types.name: Paper
types.blurb: A research result, usually on arXiv or in a journal.

types.name: Model
types.blurb: A trained model released or announced.

types.name: Product
types.blurb: Something people can use: an app, API, tool or feature.

types.name: Event
types.blurb: A moment: a match, a launch, a law, a prize, a deal.

types.name: Person
types.blurb: A move or milestone of a person who shapes the field.

types.name: Concept
types.blurb: An idea or technique with a name.

eras.name: Foundations
eras.blurb: Artificial neurons, the Turing test and a summer workshop that named the field.

eras.name: Winters and expert systems
eras.blurb: Funding cuts, hand-written rules, and backpropagation quietly arriving.

eras.name: Statistical learning
eras.blurb: Learning from data beats writing rules. Big datasets and GPUs appear.

eras.name: Deep learning
eras.blurb: AlexNet wins ImageNet and deep neural networks take over vision, speech and games.

eras.name: Transformers and scale
eras.blurb: Attention replaces recurrence, and bigger models keep getting better.

eras.name: Generative boom
eras.blurb: ChatGPT reaches the public. Every company ships a chatbot.

eras.name: Agents and reasoning
eras.blurb: Models think before answering, use tools, and act on computers.

layers.name: Math and neurons
layers.blurb: The arithmetic underneath: neurons, gradients, probability.

layers.name: Learning methods
layers.blurb: How a system learns: from labels, from rewards, from raw data.

layers.name: Architectures
layers.blurb: The shape of the network: convolutions, recurrence, attention.

layers.name: Models
layers.blurb: Trained systems and families of them.

layers.name: Training and alignment
layers.blurb: Making models capable, then making them helpful and safe.

layers.name: Building with AI
layers.blurb: Prompts, RAG, tools, agents and protocols that turn models into products.

layers.name: Evaluation and safety
layers.blurb: Measuring what models can do and keeping them in bounds.

layers.name: Infrastructure
layers.blurb: Chips, serving and compression that make it all run.

layers.name: Data and BI
layers.blurb: Where AI meets analytics: semantic models, Fabric, Copilot in Power BI.

labs.name: OpenAI
labs.blurb: Maker of GPT, ChatGPT, DALL-E and the o-series reasoning models.

labs.name: Anthropic
labs.blurb: Maker of Claude. Known for Constitutional AI and the Model Context Protocol.

labs.name: Google and DeepMind
labs.blurb: Transformer, BERT, AlphaGo, AlphaFold and Gemini.

labs.name: Microsoft and GitHub
labs.blurb: ResNet, LoRA, GitHub Copilot, Microsoft 365 Copilot, Fabric and Power BI.

labs.name: Meta
labs.blurb: FAIR research, PyTorch and the open-weight Llama family.

labs.name: Mistral AI
labs.blurb: Paris lab known for small, efficient open-weight models.

labs.name: DeepSeek
labs.blurb: Chinese lab whose open R1 model matched frontier reasoning at low cost.

labs.name: Qwen (Alibaba)
labs.blurb: Alibaba's open-weight model family, widely used for local and fine-tuned models.

labs.name: NVIDIA
labs.blurb: GPUs and CUDA, the hardware layer most AI runs on.

labs.name: IBM
labs.blurb: Deep Blue, Watson, and early machine learning research.

labs.name: Safe Superintelligence
labs.blurb: Ilya Sutskever's lab, focused on one goal: safe superintelligence.

labs.name: Academia
labs.blurb: Universities and independent researchers, where most foundations came from.

labs.name: Governments
labs.blurb: Laws, summits and public funding that shape the field.

labs.name: Others
labs.blurb: Everyone else: startups, open-source projects and independent builders.
